issues.text: Under О21 as decided («the failure message names that row's path and its rule»), the design's own HC-7c form (design E11.2, the four literal `assert.ok(!has(…, "H4"))` calls as built on its trial) does not meet criterion 8 for row 21: prettier splits that call over three lines, and node's generated message for a split `assert.ok(` shows only «assert.ok(», so the output names neither the path nor H4 (rows 117-119, on one line each, are named). The same trial with an explicit message on each of the four assertions meets every probe (T1 literal calls, T2 a loop, both measured). So «the design's trial passes» holds after one change of the design, not as built: CODE-DESIGNER (run M0DOCS-20261117-01, 1b) adds to E11.2 a message naming the file and the rule to each `!has` assertion, or ORCH reads О21 otherwise. The criterion was not softened to fit the trial.

Consequences of О21 in criterion 8: a plain loop without a message is refused again (the gate's V8), so F4 of M0BACKLOG step 02 holds only for a loop whose message names the file and the rule; and a test that pins the order of the base (W12, accepted by the old greps) is refused by the order control (i'') by О21's own words.

Beyond the named mutants, in the class of F1: my step-01 probes also accepted W11 (the count assertion replaced by a pin on R1), which the tag's greps refused. The step-1b form refuses it (the static name check, the twin (i') and the 111 probe that adds R1' instead of a second R1); the old «R1 written twice» probe is replaced by «E with R1'» for that reason.

О23's later re-check goes by the commit that brought the line. It is true only if the release commit holds docs/requirements.yaml and docs/issues/ as they were when the lines were read. With the release together with M0.13 (design О14), records of other runs that land between DOC-UPDATER's step-10 refresh and the release commit make the lines false at their own commit, and a later re-check is red. ORCH should keep the step-10 refresh right before the release commit. The method found exactly this on the old README: its «Open defects: 74» was 73 at its own commit (self_check S6).

My own slips, each seen and redone: an `echo` of equals signs in zsh stopped one command list (AP-156 item 2), redone in bash; `set -u` with an optional argument in my probe script, fixed before any result was used; `PIPESTATUS` printed nothing under zsh, so the format check was rerun alone for its exit code. No command was denied by the permission check in this step.
